hypothesis: Hoisted m_mask/n_mask with single k_off and explicit tl.range num_stages=3 pipelining will outperform the baseline K-loop by reducing per-iteration mask arithmetic for tl.load A/B and improving overlap of tl.load A/B pointer increments with tl.dot accumulation on 512x3072x768 FP16 with 64x128x32 tiles.
expected_mechanism: Compute m_mask and n_mask once outside the loop and reuse them in tl.load A mask, tl.load B mask, and final tl.store mask instead of rebuilding m<M and n<N each iteration. Compute k_off = offset*BK once per iteration instead of two offset*BK expressions in A and B K-predicates. Hoist loop_k = tl.cdiv(K, BK) and iterate with tl.range(0, loop_k, num_stages=3) to give the software pipeliner an explicit depth matching the launcher to overlap cp.async tl.load from a_ptrs/b_ptrs with tl.dot FP32 accumulation, while a_ptrs += BK and b_ptrs += BK*N pointer advances preserve coalescing. No math, tile, FP16 I/O, or launch change.
reasoning_from_feedback: This differs from both prior generated attempts and reviewed structural kernels and claims no measured feedback for unevaluated code. The prior unevaluated GROUP_M=4 candidate and rejected GROUP_M=8 candidate changed only program-ID remapping and, for the rejected one, EVEN mask elimination with AnnAssign syntax; this proposal keeps baseline direct 2D pid_m/pid_n mapping with no GROUP_M swizzle and uses only plain assignments. It differs from reviewed structural grouped_m4 CTA ordering and split_k K-parallel reduction by leaving grid, single launch, and reduction structure unchanged and instead reorganizing inner K-loop computation, mask reuse, pointer predicate formation, and tl.load/tl.dot pipeline depth. The prior candidate status is not compiled, checked for correctness, or timed, so no speedup or correctness is inferred from it.
